items.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022
items.q: the local rabbi’s last name was Tykoski

ctx.x: Well said. I was pleased to read about this project in Poland that came about because of this fellow who was trying to help Michael out. Can you just tell me a little about that?

Well his name is Wlodek Pawlik and he’s the head of an exceptional musical family. His brother — I mean his son is a wonderful musician. His wife is also a pianist and composer as is Wlodek. And because they’re of Eastern European and Polish descent and our family is also from that area, Mike and people working with him put out feelers to try to get a match for his cancer. It was an area called Tykocin. And our family name on my mother’s side is similar, Tykoski, and the rabbi, the local rabbi’s last name was…

reasons he went into such decline as his daughter was a half match. They’re called alleles and the need a match of I think 12 matches. They tried what was called a Haplo identical transplant but it didn’t work. You have to find someone with a match. So Susan, Mike’s wife — getting off the subject here — has spent many years trying to get people to register and register their blood just for this because it’s still a shortage, particularly minorities. And I don’t understand all the science behind it but that’s what…
